nodes.label: piSignage player API log download path traversal (before 2.6.4)
nodes.precondition: Remote access to piSignage web application component before 2.6.4; attacker authenticated as a low-privilege user; api/settings/log?file= endpoint reachable; file parameter accepts path traversal sequences such as ../; target Raspberry Pi filesystem readable by the web application process.
nodes.postcondition: Arbitrary file download from Raspberry Pi filesystem via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal; disclosure of sensitive files and logs; potential exposure of credentials or configuration on the Raspberry Pi host.

nodes.label: Oculus Browser UI HTML injection (5.2.7 through before 5.7.11)
nodes.precondition: Victim uses affected Oculus Browser version >=5.2.7 and <5.7.11; remote web page is visited or loaded; Oculus Browser UI fails to sanitize injected HTML.
nodes.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML code injected into Oculus Browser UI; attacker can spoof UI; potential code execution in the Oculus Browser/UI context.

nodes.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe privileged arbitrary file write via hard link to log file (before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows)
nodes.precondition: Local access to Windows host with vulnerable Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849; attacker is an unprivileged local user; attacker can create a hard link to a log file targeted by privileged OVRRedir.exe; OVRRedir.exe runs with privileges and writes to the file.
nodes.postcondition: Privileged OVRRedir.exe writes to an arbitrary file; unprivileged local user gains arbitrary file write as a privileged process; local privilege escalation on Windows.

nodes.label: RaspAP 2.5 includes/webconsole.php unrestricted web console command execution
nodes.precondition: Authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5; includes/webconsole.php is exposed; web console is misconfigured and virtually unrestricted; underlying Raspberry Pi OS is reachable through the web console.
nodes.postcondition: Command execution on underlying Raspberry Pi OS; ability to upload files; execution of code on the Raspberry Pi host.

nodes.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher.exe privileged handle exposure local privilege escalation (after 1.39 and before 31.1.0.67.507)
nodes.precondition: Local access to Windows host with affected Oculus Desktop version >1.39 and <31.1.0.67.507; attacker controls an unprivileged process; OVRServiceLauncher.exe handle management bug is reachable.
nodes.postcondition: Privileged process handle exposed to an unprivileged process; local privilege escalation.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi 3 B+/4 B Glowworm LED power side-channel speech recovery (through 2021-08-09)
nodes.precondition: Raspberry Pi 3 B+ or 4 B device through 2021-08-09; specific use case where the device supplies power to audio-output equipment/speakers; audio/speech is played through the speakers; attacker has remote optical observation with a telescope and an electro-optical sensor directed at the power indicator LED; LED intensity correlates to power consumption.
nodes.postcondition: Recover speech signals/sound played by the speakers by analyzing electro-optical measurements of the power indicator LED; confidentiality breach of audio information.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 default pi account password unchanged
nodes.precondition: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10; default password for the pi account has not been changed; attacker can reach an authentication surface for the pi account (SSH, console, or other exposed service).
nodes.postcondition: Attacker authenticates as the pi account; gains administrator privileges (sudo/root-level control) on Raspberry Pi OS.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Jetson Linux IOMMU misconfiguration PCI bus direct memory access
nodes.precondition: NVIDIA Jetson Linux distribution with vulnerable IOMMU configuration; attacker is unprivileged but has physical access to the board; attacker can access the PCI bus.
nodes.postcondition: Direct read/write access to the entire system address space through the PCI bus; denial of service; code execution; escalation of privileges; impact to data integrity and confidentiality; scope impact may extend to other components.

edges.label: Default pi account administrator privileges on Raspberry Pi OS can provide or bypass authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5 web console, satisfying RaspAP's authenticated access precondition.
Administrator privileges on Raspberry Pi OS can disclose or modify piSignage credentials/configuration, satisfying authenticated low-privilege user access to piSignage before 2.6.4.

Command execution on underlying Raspberry Pi OS via RaspAP 2.5 web console can create, modify, or recover piSignage low-privilege user credentials, satisfying authenticated access to piSignage player API.
Arbitrary file download from Raspberry Pi filesystem via piSignage path traversal may disclose RaspAP configuration or credentials, satisfying authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5.
